2d33cc1987ca: Can guests book on a Salesforce Experience Cloud site without logging in?
1064c966a53d: Yes. MultiDatePick Resource Booking is a Lightning Web Component (LWC) you drop on any Experience Cloud page, including a public one. Guests pick a resource, a day and an open time slot without logging in, and each booking saves as a record in your own org, with capacity and conflict checks before Save.
f3dc0427cada: Can I limit seats per session for public bookings?
b2c6cf4c1fbe: Yes. Give the resource a capacity, such as 12 seats, and every time slot shows a live badge like 3/12. A full slot cannot be picked, so a public session never takes more bookings than it has seats. Minimum notice, buffers and closures apply to guests too.
6bb74d652be3: Can a guest user edit or cancel a booking?
6625342cd6b9: No. Salesforce lets guest users read and create records but never edit or delete them, on every app. If a guest tries to move a booking, MultiDatePick explains why instead of failing quietly. Put edit and cancel on a member site where people log in.
70b1a4ebbaf0: Does it work on a member site with logins?
42e604e91c52: Yes. Logged-in members book under their own permissions, so editing, cancelling and per-person calendars driven by a Screen Flow all work there.
45064ff8ccdb: Do I need Apex or an external scheduling tool?
9d72d39fbf6c: No. Build the booking setup in the Setup Wizard, drag the Resource Booking component onto the page in Experience Builder and set Config Name. Bookings save as records on your own Salesforce objects.
b097b2d911f6: Where is the booking data stored?
7383884cd233: In your Salesforce org, on the objects you choose. MultiDatePick is 100% native: no external servers, and nothing is synced to another vendor.
